title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
summary: The airline says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless there is an end to the US-Israel war with Iran.

title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts a missile as fighting rages in Yemen’s al-Jawf
summary: Houthi-affiliated media report that seven people were wounded in strikes on the city of Hodeidah.

title: Nuclear radiation in Russia, Ukraine? No, just hacked warning alerts
summary: Warnings startle people in Ukraine, but authorities say they cleared up the confusion in under an hour.

title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
summary: The country was the first to contribute troops to the AU mission established to stabilise Somalia in 2007.

title: Anthrax outbreak kills hippos in DR Congo’s Virunga National Park
summary: Drought and conflict compound the threat to wildlife in eastern DR Congo.

title: NBA: Yaxel Lendeborg scores 37 as Warriors defeat Clippers
summary: Golden State Warriors' rookie leads scoring in 124-112 win over Los Angeles Clippers, while Celtics beat Magic 108-97.

title: Bangladesh garment factories disrupted as protests continue for third day
summary: Workers in Bangladesh's largest export sector are demanding a minimum wage increase amid rising inflation.

title: Iran killed her teenage daughter - now she is facing up to the regime
summary: Samira's 16-year-old daughter Sevda was shot dead as they took part in mass protests in January.

title: France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police
summary: There were hundreds of arrests as protesters took to the streets in cities across France for the third weekend in a row.

title: Peaceful protests in Germany spiral into violence and looting
summary: Thousands joined largely orderly demonstrations earlier in the day, before violence erupted in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.

title: Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack
summary: The new police unit is a security measure in response to last year's deadly shooting attack at a Hanukkah festival.

title: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent
summary: The protests in cities across Germany - including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt - came on the same day hundreds of thousands also protested in France.

title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials
summary: The order comes after election officials received letters demanding they set aside the ballots of possible non-citizen voters.

title: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
summary: More than 320,000 people demonstrated across France against the rising cost of living and poor public services, with clashes between some protesters and police.

title: World News in Brief: 300,000 displaced in Lebanon, Türk ‘deeply concerned’ over Novaya Gazeta closure, $50 million refugee appeal, World Cities Day
summary: More than 300,000 people displaced since early March remain internally displaced in Lebanon, where the humanitarian crisis is “far from over,” according to the UN’s aid coordination office (OCHA).

title: Ukraine: Oleshky ceasefire offers ‘hope’ for civilians as attacks on aid vehicles continue
summary: Each day the ceasefire in Oleshky holds means hope for civilians in the city, the UN’s top humanitarian official said, stressing that those wishing to leave must be able to do so safely and voluntarily.

title: DR Congo: Hunger deepens for millions amid conflict, Ebola and climate shocks
summary: More than 28 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are not getting enough to eat and the number is expected to tick up in the coming months, according to the latest alert from the IPC global food security monitor.

title: UN rights office warns of deepening displacement ‘nightmare’ in Gaza
summary: Israeli forces continue to push Palestinians into ever-smaller areas of the Gaza Strip while destroying civilian infrastructure and attacking displacement sites, the UN human rights office, OHCHR, warned on Friday amid concerns of ethnic cleansing.

title: Yemen war makes reaching assistance too dangerous for many
summary: More than 280,000 people have now been displaced by fighting in Yemen and many vulnerable people are unable to access lifesaving relief because it is too dangerous to do so, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Friday.

title: Myanmar’s illicit economy fuels escalating violence, with civilians bearing the brunt
summary: Myanmar’s human rights situation is “catastrophic”, the UN independent expert on the country warned at a press briefing Thursday, as the war spirals with no end in sight.

title: AI is changing the way we think. The question is whether we’ll notice in time
summary: Artificial intelligence promises to make life easier. With a few keystrokes, it can write emails, summarize reports, generate ideas and answer complex questions in seconds. For many people, it feels like a technological leap on par with the arrival of the internet itself.

title: World News in Brief: 5 children killed in Sudan, Haiti hunger emergency, Yemen war update
summary: At least five children were killed and two others injured in a drone attack on a market in Nyala, in Sudan’s South Darfur state, on Monday, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Thursday.

title: Russia drone strike on Ukrainian railway station kills 13
summary: The UN’s top humanitarian official in Ukraine on Thursday condemned a Russian drone attack on the city of Dnipro that killed at least 13 civilians and injured 10 others at its main railway station.

title: Security Council LIVE: Can new technology keep the world’s sea lanes safe?
summary: Cheap drones, autonomous vessels and cyberattacks are changing the threats to the world’s shipping lanes – and the tools to counter them. At an open debate on Thursday, the Security Council is weighing how emerging technologies could both endanger and protect seafarers, global trade and food and energy supplies.

title: UN human rights chief urges better protection of civilians in conflicts
summary: Youth-led protests against corruption and inequality in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Madagascar reflect a growing demand for reinforcing human rights around the world, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said at a press briefing on Wednesday.

title: Backing for UN call to end Cuba embargo falls to 20-year low
summary: The UN General Assembly on Wednesday called for the 34th time for an end to the US economic, commercial and financial embargo on Cuba – but with the weakest backing for the resolution in two decades.

title: Ending conflict is ‘number one thing’ to reduce world hunger, new WFP chief says
summary: Reducing conflict is the single most effective way to tackle global hunger, the new head of the UN World Food Programme (WFP), Luke Lindberg, said on Wednesday, noting that conflict drives two thirds of the acute food insecurity affecting 266 million people worldwide.

title: Protecting the storytellers: Women journalists on the frontline of conflict
summary: As online abuse, gender-based attacks and impunity ramp up the threats to women reporting from crisis zones, journalists and UN leaders are calling for urgent action to protect those who document conflict.

title: Record heat-related deaths in 2023, WHO-partnered report finds
summary: Climate inaction continues to harm and kill people in all countries with a record 710,000 estimated deaths globally from heat in 2023, a UN-partnered report warned on Wednesday. For the first time, more than seven in 10 fatalities were attributable to human-caused climate change.

title: Ocean’s ability to absorb carbon is weakening as climate change intensifies, UN warns
summary: The ocean absorbs around 30 per cent of human-caused carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions and 90 per cent of excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases. But climate change has already reduced its capacity to absorb carbon by approximately six per cent, a new UN report warns ahead of the COP31 climate conference in November.

title: General Assembly weighs US embargo against Cuba ahead of 34th vote
summary: The General Assembly opened its annual debate on the US economic embargo against Cuba on Tuesday. On Wednesday, 28 October, Member States will vote for the 34th time on a resolution calling for it to end.
